title: Moving averages and choosing with RMSE
summary: Why smooth the data, the 3-period moving average formula, the 2026 forecast, the 5-period moving average, and picking the method with the lower RMSE.

chunks.heading: Why smooth the data?
chunks.explanation_md:
Historical data contain two things: an **underlying pattern** and **random fluctuations**.

Fitting a **trend line** captures the pattern, but it **imposes** a particular mathematical shape (linear or quadratic) on the data. If you do not want to assume a shape, you can **smooth** the data instead: a **moving average** averages the most recent observations.
chunks.exam_line: Trend lines impose a shape; moving averages smooth the data by averaging recent observations.

check_questions.stem: Fitting a trend line imposes a particular mathematical pattern on the data.

chunks.big_idea: A moving average smooths out random ups and downs without forcing a line or curve onto the data.
chunks.exam_answer_md: Historical data contain an underlying pattern and random fluctuations. Trend lines impose a mathematical pattern; a **moving average** instead smooths the data by averaging the most recent observations.

chunks.heading: The 3-period moving average
chunks.explanation_md:
The forecast for next period is the **average of a fixed number of recent periods**. For three periods:

**F(t+1) = (Y(t) + Y(t-1) + Y(t-2)) / 3**

It **smooths random fluctuations**, is **easy to calculate** and uses **recent observations**.

| Year | Actual sales | 3-year MA forecast |
|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 100 | 85 |
| 2021 | 120 | 91.67 |
| 2022 | 110 | 103.33 |
| 2023 | 130 | 110 |
| 2024 | 140 | 120 |
| 2025 | 150 | 126.67 |
| 2026 | | **140** |

The 2026 forecast is the average of 2023, 2024 and 2025: (130 + 140 + 150) / 3 = **140**.

chunks.heading: 3 or 5 periods? Compare the RMSE
chunks.explanation_md:
A **5-year moving average** averages five years instead of three; its 2026 forecast is **130**.

To choose, compute the **root mean square error** for each and pick the **lower** one:

**RMSE = square root of [sum of (At - Ft)² / n]**, where n is the number of periods that have a forecast.

| | Sum of (A - F)² | n | RMSE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-year MA | 2416.367 | 6 | **20.068** |
| 5-year MA | 2866 | 4 | **26.767** |

Since RMSE3 < RMSE5, the **3-year moving average** is preferred, so the 2026 forecast is **140**.
chunks.exam_line: RMSE = square root of [sum of (At - Ft)² / n]; pick the lower: 20.068 for the 3-year MA beats 26.767, so forecast 140.

questions.stem: The 5-year moving average forecast for 2026 is:
Annual sales for 2017 to 2025 are 80, 85, 90, 100, 120, 110, 130, 140 and 150. Find the forecast for 2026 using a 3-year moving average, and use RMSE to compare it with a 5-year moving average.
questions.model_answer_md:
**3-year MA forecasts** (average of the previous three years): 2020: 85, 2021: 91.67, 2022: 103.33, 2023: 110, 2024: 120, 2025: 126.67, and **2026: (130 + 140 + 150) / 3 = 140**.

**RMSE** = square root of [sum of (At - Ft)² / n]:

| | Sum of (A - F)² | n | RMSE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3-year MA | 2416.367 | 6 | 20.068 |
| 5-year MA | 2866 | 4 | 26.767 |

The 3-year MA has the lower RMSE, so it is preferred and the forecast for 2026 is **140**.
